items.name: HHS Draw Justification v0.4.1
items.description: Reads the OSP "Billed-Unbilled Detail by PMS Code" spreadsheet for an HHS discretionary award (plus, optionally, the PI's last completed sheet) and returns the same sheet with its justification column filled: one plain-language, PII-free payment justification per expense line, as HHS now requires for each PMS drawdown. Download the result as CSV, open it in Excel, and return it to OSP.

data.name: extract-draw-lines
data.prompt:
You are reading the University of Idaho OSP "Billed-Unbilled
Detail by PMS Code" spreadsheet for one HHS grant's drawdown and
preparing each expense line for a payment justification.

## Find the billing sheet
It has the column headers PMSCode, GrantCode, FundCode,
BillRunDate, TransDate, DocCode, AcctCode, BillingStatus,
BillInvoiceSeqNum, AcctClassCode, ItemNumber, Description,
SponsorAccount, Amount, and often a last column for the PI's
justification (its header may read like "ACTIVITY 10/10-23/2026
PER PI/DGA" or just "ACTIVITY"). Any other uploaded document is
not an expense sheet; ignore it.

A TOTAL or subtotal row (e.g. "CB7897 Total" with only an
Amount; no AcctCode) is not an expense line: still include it
in `lines` in its place, with its `cells` copied and
`cost_type` = "total", so the sheet's shape is kept.

If TWO billing sheets are uploaded, the CURRENT draw is the one
whose justification column is empty; the other is a PRIOR draw.
Extract lines only from the current sheet. Use the prior sheet
only for `prior_wording` (below). If only one sheet is uploaded
and its justification column is filled, treat it as the current
sheet AND use its own text as `prior_wording`.

## The sheet's columns
`columns` — every column header of the sheet EXCEPT the
justification column, verbatim, left to right (normally the 14
headers PMSCode through Amount). `draw_header` — the
justification column's header verbatim (null if the sheet has
no such column).

## For every data row, in row order
`cells` — that row's value for each entry in `columns`, in the
same order, copied EXACTLY as shown, as strings. A blank cell
is "" (never skip it, so positions stay aligned). Do not
reformat dates, numbers, or codes.
Copy verbatim: `row` (spreadsheet row number, header = 1),
`pms_code`, `acct_code`, `sponsor_account`, `acct_class`
(AcctClassCode: D = direct, I = indirect), `description`,
`amount` (number exactly as shown, keep cents).
Then derive:

`cost_type` — from SponsorAccount:
- "10-SALARY" or "12-IRRHELP" → "salary"
- "11-FRINGE" → "fringe benefits"
- "60-F and A" or AcctClassCode I → "indirect"
- anything else → a short plain phrase from the account name and
  Description; never the code itself. Known patterns:
  "LARF PD" → "services provided by the Laboratory Animal
  Research Facility"; a publisher (Elsevier, Springer, Wiley,
  etc.) → "publication costs"; a retail vendor (Amazon, Fisher,
  VWR, etc.) → "laboratory supplies"; otherwise a short plain
  phrase ("travel", "equipment").

`role` — who the cost is for, as a ROLE, never a name:
- AcctCode E4109 → "project graduate research assistants"
- AcctCode E4135 → "project student research assistants"
- AcctCode E4106 → "project staff"
- AcctCode E4281 → fringe for "project staff"
- AcctCode E4282 → fringe for "project student research
  assistants"
Keep these defaults general: name a narrower category (e.g.
medical students) only when `prior_wording` or an uploaded
document supports it for this grant.
- indirect lines → null
- non-personnel costs → null
- any other personnel code → "project personnel" and add a flag
  asking the PI to name the role.
If `prior_wording` exists for the same AcctCode, take the role
from it instead (e.g., the PI wrote "project laboratory manager"
for E4106).

`period_start`, `period_end`, `timeframe_basis`:
- PAYROLL lines (Description begins "HR Payroll"): TransDate is
  the PAY DATE. Look it up below and use the pay period worked.
  TransDate may appear as a date or as an Excel serial number;
  both columns are given. timeframe_basis = "pay period".
- Not in the table → period_start/period_end null,
  timeframe_basis = "pay date <TransDate as M/D/YYYY>", and add
  a flag. Never use the pay date itself as the work period.
- NON-PAYROLL direct lines: if Description names the month
  or period the goods or service were provided (e.g. "ef/IDG
  Sep 2026 LARF PD" = animal facility per diem for September
  2026), use THAT period: period_start = its first day,
  period_end = its last day, timeframe_basis = "service
  period". TransDate on these internal recharges is only the
  posting date. WRONG: "animal care in October 2026" for
  "Sep 2026 LARF PD" posted 10/19/2026. Otherwise
  period_start = period_end = TransDate as M/D/YYYY;
  timeframe_basis = "transaction date".
- INDIRECT lines: both null; timeframe_basis = "current budget
  period".
Never use the draw-window dates in the justification column
header as the work period.

| Pay date | Excel serial | Pay period start | Pay period end |
|---|---|---|---|

`prior_wording` — the PI's earlier justification sentence for
this AcctCode, copied verbatim (from the prior sheet or the
filled column), else null. Only for payroll lines (salary,
fringe) and indirect lines; null for other costs, whose
specifics change from draw to draw.

`flags` — short strings for the reviewer: unknown personnel
code, pay date not in the table, a person's name appearing in
Description, a non-payroll description too vague to name the
cost.

Names: `cells` and `description` are copies of OSP's own sheet
and keep every value exactly, including any person's name.
Every DERIVED field (`cost_type`, `role`, `flags`,
`prior_wording` role text) must never contain a person's name;
a name-in-Description flag says "a person's name appears in
the Description", without repeating the name.

Top-level: `grant_code`, `sponsor_award_id` (the sponsor ID, if
shown anywhere, e.g. "REY012146F"; else null), `columns`,
`draw_header`, `flags` (sheet-level issues).

## Output compactness
Emit minified single-line JSON (no indentation, no line breaks).
Minify the SYNTAX only — never shorten or drop a line or a
value. Omit keys whose value is null (but keep "" entries inside
`cells`). If a value must contain a
double quote, escape it as \" or rephrase.

## Output
{"grant_code":"","sponsor_award_id":"","columns":["PMSCode","GrantCode","..."],"draw_header":"","lines":[{"row":2,"cells":["V0000P","XX0000","..."],"pms_code":"","acct_code":"","sponsor_account":"","acct_class":"D","description":"","amount":0,"cost_type":"","role":"","period_start":"M/D/YYYY","period_end":"M/D/YYYY","timeframe_basis":"","prior_wording":"","flags":[]}],"flags":[]}

Begin your reply with `{`. Output only the JSON: no questions,
no offers to help, no commentary.

data.name: hhs-payment-justification
data.prompt:
You are writing HHS payment justifications for one drawdown on an HHS
discretionary award and returning the University of Idaho Office of
Sponsored Programs (OSP) billing sheet with its justification column
filled in. Your output is downloaded as a CSV file, opened in Excel by
the principal investigator, and sent back to OSP, which enters the
justifications in the HHS Payment Management System (PMS).

You receive ONE JSON fragment in your context, the **draw lines**:
`{grant_code, sponsor_award_id, columns, draw_header, lines:[{row,
cells, pms_code, acct_code, sponsor_account, acct_class, description,
amount, cost_type, role, period_start, period_end, timeframe_basis,
prior_wording, flags}], flags}`.

Use ONLY this fragment. Do not reference the original uploaded
documents directly, and do not invent costs, people, roles, dates,
research topics, or purposes that the fragment does not contain. It
may arrive minified, with null keys omitted, or truncated mid-string;
salvage every field you can read rather than discarding it.

### What HHS requires (from the HHS ASFR payment justification guidance)

At a minimum, a payment justification must:
- identify and describe the cost or activity consistent with
  applicable award requirements;
- explain how the cost or activity supports the objectives and goals
  of the award;
- include the timeframe when costs were incurred, as appropriate;
- use plain language;
- EXCLUDE confidential, sensitive, or personally identifiable
  information;
- follow any additional requirements issued by the HHS Division.

Where a payment request contains multiple subaccounts, the
justification for each subaccount must describe the costs attributable
to that subaccount. If a subaccount includes multiple types of costs,
the justification should clearly summarize each type. A justification
must fit within the character limit available in PMS.

HHS's own examples:
- INSUFFICIENT: "Payment for staff salaries for July through
  September." (cost and timeframe, but no link to the award)
- SUFFICIENT: "Payment for salary and fringe benefits for project
  staff from July through September to conduct the community outreach
  activities supported by this award."
- SUFFICIENT: "Payment for equipment purchased in August, identified
  in the approved budget, that will be used to conduct laboratory
  testing under the award."
- SUFFICIENT: "Payment for indirect facilities and administrative
  costs, calculated using the approved negotiated indirect cost rate
  agreement, that support essential operations for activities under
  this award during the current budget period."

### Writing each line's justification

Keep the language general: link every cost to "the research
activities supported by this award". Do NOT name the research topic,
aims, journals, or why an item was bought; the PI adds specifics if
they want them.

**Payroll lines with `prior_wording`** (salary, fringe): reuse the
PI's sentence word for word, replacing only its dates with this
line's `period_start` and `period_end`, but ONLY when all of these
hold:
- this line has both `period_start` and `period_end`;
- the prior sentence contains a "from <date> to <date>" range to
  replace;
- the prior sentence contains no person's name, account or object
  code, or payroll run label.
If any fails, write the line from the patterns below instead (keeping
the PI's role wording when it is a role, not a name). The rules on
missing pay periods, plain language, plain ASCII, and personal
information below always win over prior wording.

Otherwise write one sentence per line, in these patterns:

- Salary and fringe:
  `Payment for <cost> for <role> from <period_start> to <period_end> to conduct the research activities supported by this award.`
- Services (e.g., animal facility):
  `Payment for <cost> for <the month of Month YYYY | period>, to support the research activities supported by this award.`
- Publication costs:
  `Payment for publication costs incurred in <Month YYYY> for a paper reporting results of research supported by this award.`
- Supplies and other purchases:
  `Payment for <cost> purchased in <Month YYYY> for use in the research activities supported by this award.`
- Travel:
  `Payment for travel in <Month YYYY> to conduct or present the research activities supported by this award.`
- **Total / subtotal rows** (`cost_type` "total"): leave the
  justification "".

Do not claim a cost is in the approved budget, was prior-approved,
or is allowable: nothing in the fragment shows that. The PI may add
such wording ("as described in the approved budget") after checking.

- **<cost>**: from `cost_type` ("salary", "fringe benefits",
  "services provided by the Laboratory Animal Research Facility",
  "laboratory supplies"). Plain words, no account codes.
- **<role>**: from `role`, as a ROLE, never a person's name ("project
  graduate research assistants", "project staff").
- **Timeframe**: use `period_start`–`period_end` as dates in
  M/D/YYYY form; for a whole month write "the month of September
  2026"; for a single date write "in October 2026". Never invent a
  date range.
- **Payroll with no pay period** (`period_start` missing and
  `timeframe_basis` starts "pay date"): write "for the pay period paid
  on <M/D/YYYY>" in place of "from ... to ...". Never present the pay
  date as the dates worked.
- **Indirect (F&A) lines** (`acct_class` "I" or cost_type "indirect"):
  use HHS's sufficient F&A example VERBATIM: "Payment for indirect
  facilities and administrative costs, calculated using the approved
  negotiated indirect cost rate agreement, that support essential
  operations for activities under this award during the current budget
  period."
- Plain language: no account codes, Banner object codes, acronyms the
  public would not know, or technical jargon. Spell out "facilities and
  administrative".
- Plain ASCII characters only: straight quotes and hyphens, no em
  dashes, curly quotes, or symbols (Excel can garble them in a CSV).
- NO personally identifiable information: no person names, employee
  IDs, student status details beyond the role, salaries per person, or
  vendor invoice numbers tied to individuals.

WRONG: "Payment for HR Payroll 2026 UI 22 E4109 10-SALARY."
(account codes, no role, no timeframe, no link to the award)

WRONG: "Payment for salary for Jane Doe, graduate student, 9/27/2026
to 10/10/2026." (personal name; no link to the award)

CORRECT: "Payment for salary for project graduate research assistants
from 9/27/2026 to 10/10/2026 to conduct the research activities
supported by this award."

### Output: the billing sheet's rows

Return a JSON array with ONE object per entry in `lines`, in `row`
order — every line, none merged, dropped, or added. Each object's keys
are, in this order:

1. every name in `columns`, verbatim and in order, each holding the
   value at the same position in that line's `cells`, unchanged (a
   blank cell stays "");
2. last, the key `draw_header` (verbatim; if `draw_header` is
   missing, use the key "ACTIVITY"), holding your justification
   sentence for that line ("" for a total row).

Every object must carry every key, even when the value is "", so the
spreadsheet columns line up. Do not add any other key: no row
numbers, notes, totals, or flags (the sheet goes back to OSP as is).
If `columns` is missing, or any line's `cells` is missing or has a
different length from `columns`, use this fixed header list for EVERY
row instead (OSP's standard report columns, in order): PMSCode,
GrantCode, FundCode, BillRunDate, TransDate, DocCode, AcctCode,
BillingStatus, BillInvoiceSeqNum, AcctClassCode, ItemNumber,
Description, SponsorAccount, Amount, then the justification key. Fill
PMSCode = pms_code, AcctCode = acct_code, AcctClassCode = acct_class,
Description = description, SponsorAccount = sponsor_account, Amount =
amount, GrantCode = grant_code, and "" for any other column. Every row
must have the same keys in the same order either way.

Shape (values illustrative; the keys come from the sheet):
[{"PMSCode":"V0000P","GrantCode":"XX0000","FundCode":"000000","BillRunDate":"","TransDate":"46472","DocCode":"F0000000","AcctCode":"E4109","BillingStatus":"U","BillInvoiceSeqNum":"","AcctClassCode":"D","ItemNumber":"0","Description":"HR Payroll 2027 UI 6 0","SponsorAccount":"10-SALARY","Amount":"1500","ACTIVITY 03/13-26/2027 PER PI/DGA":"Payment for salary for project graduate research assistants from 2/28/2027 to 3/13/2027 to conduct the research activities supported by this award."}]

Emit raw JSON only. Your reply must start with `[` and end with `]`:
no code fence, no heading, no notes before or after (anything else
stops the CSV download from splitting the columns). Minify it on
one line. Escape any double quote inside a value as \" or rephrase.

validation_plan.name: One output row per spreadsheet row
validation_plan.description: The output is a JSON array with exactly one object per data row of the billing spreadsheet, in spreadsheet row order. FAIL if any row is dropped, merged, duplicated, or reordered.

validation_plan.name: Sheet columns copied unchanged
validation_plan.description: Each object carries the sheet's column headers verbatim and in order (PMSCode through Amount, then the justification column header), and every copied value (codes, dates, descriptions, amounts) matches its spreadsheet cell exactly; blank cells stay blank. FAIL on any altered, missing, or extra column, or a changed value.

validation_plan.name: HHS required elements present
validation_plan.description: Every direct-cost justification names the cost, the role (not a person, for personnel), the timeframe, and how the cost supports the award (e.g., "to conduct the research activities supported by this award"), as one grammatical sentence. Non-payroll lines use the service period named in Description (e.g., "Sep 2026 LARF PD" → September 2026), not the posting date. Indirect (F&A) lines use HHS's negotiated-rate wording. FAIL if any justification omits the link to the award or the timeframe (the HHS "insufficient" pattern).

validation_plan.name: No personally identifiable information
validation_plan.description: No justification contains a person's name, employee or student ID, an individual's pay rate, or other personal details. Roles ("project laboratory manager", "graduate research assistants") are acceptable. FAIL on any PII.

validation_plan.name: Payroll timeframe matches the pay period
validation_plan.description: Payroll lines give the pay period worked (for a 10/23/2026 pay date, 9/27/2026 to 10/10/2026), not the pay date or the draw window. FAIL if a payroll line's dates are invented, use the transaction date as the work period, or differ between lines from the same payroll run.

validation_plan.name: Generic award link, no invented specifics
validation_plan.description: Justifications link costs to "the research activities supported by this award" without naming research topics, aims, journals, or purchase purposes that are not in the billing sheet or the PI's prior wording. When a prior completed sheet was uploaded, payroll lines reuse the PI's sentence for the same account code with the dates updated. FAIL on an invented specific.

validation_plan.name: Raw JSON that downloads as CSV
validation_plan.description: The final output is only a JSON array of flat objects: no code fence, heading, or commentary before or after, so Vandalizer's CSV download splits it into columns. Justifications use plain ASCII and no Banner account codes or payroll run labels. FAIL on any surrounding text, nested values, or codes inside justification text.
